summary: Verified security fixes and re-ran full backend regression + public UI smoke. 13/14 pytest tests pass. CORS is now correctly locked to allow-list (no wildcard-with-credentials, evil origin not reflected). Hostinger PHP export now uses password_verify() only and schema.sql contains real bcrypt hashes (both via /package and inside the zip). All banking flows (login all 3 roles, accounts/cards/transfer/FD/loan/admin overview/RBI reports) still pass. However, brute-force lockout is NOT triggering at 5 attempts — it only fires after ~10 attempts because request.client.host varies behind the k8s ingress, splitting the IP+email identifier counter. Public / and /rates pages render with PublicNavbar and correct content; no console errors.

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout does NOT fire at 5 failed attempts as required. Observed remaining-attempt counter: 4,4,3,3,2,1,0 over 7 tries, meaning fails are being split across different identifiers. Root cause: identifier = f'{request.client.host}:{email}' but behind the ingress/proxy `request.client.host` reflects the immediate upstream (varies between requests / behind LB) instead of the real client IP. Real client IP must be read from X-Forwarded-For (first value) — or drop IP and lock on email alone. Currently a determined attacker can double the effective attempts before lockout.

action_items: Fix brute-force lockout identifier: derive client IP from `X-Forwarded-For` header (first entry, trimmed) with fallback to request.client.host, OR use email-only identifier. Recommended: `client_ip = (request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for') or '').split(',')[0].strip() or (request.client.host if request.client else '0.0.0.0')`. After the fix, re-verify that the 6th attempt returns 429 within the same test run.

rca of the issue: The brute-force lockout uses `request.client.host` which in FastAPI/Starlette returns the socket peer address (i.e., the k8s ingress/proxy), not the true client IP. Because the ingress may terminate on different upstream sockets/pods across requests, or the reported host varies, each failed login can be recorded under a different identifier string, so the count per identifier stays below 5 for longer than intended. Empirically the counter increments about once every 1.5 real attempts, so lockout fires around attempt #10 instead of #6. Mitigation: parse `X-Forwarded-For` (first IP) — standard behind Emergent's ingress — before composing the identifier, and apply the same fix to the audit_logs 'ip' field.
